lastCommit.message:
OTA-1880 — the constraint teaches its own door

OTA-1878 gave the transcript a door and never mentioned it. When the narrative
panel is measured too small to read from, EXPAND appears in the scene rail — and
that is the exact moment the player is staring at a squeezed transcript rather
than auditing the header for a key that was not there a second ago. OTA-1879 then
took ~40pt of air out of the roll, which reduces the pressure but does not
introduce the door. The owner's principle: THE CONSTRAINT SHOULD SURFACE ITS OWN
ESCAPE HATCH.

THE TRIGGER IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE PHONE. It is OTA-1878's own
`isNarrativeConstrained(feedH)` — the height the feed panel actually reported
through onLayout — and nothing else: no device model, no platform test, no window
size, no second heuristic. A large phone whose feed is genuinely squeezed (the
keyboard up, a roll open) IS taught; a small phone whose feed still reads four
lines is NOT. The derivation was hoisted above the teaching slot so the rail's key
and the card read ONE boolean and can never disagree about whether the feed is
tight.

AND THE SMALLEST HONEST IMPLEMENTATION WAS ALREADY IN THE REPO. OTA-1738 built the
teaching system this needs: one card per beat through `useTeachingSlot`, copy in
`teachingRegistry`, per-install dismissal in `useFirstTimeHint`, a global tips
kill-switch, and a replay listing in Settings → GUIDANCE. So the whole package is
ONE registry entry and ONE candidate line — no new component, no new persistence,
no new timer, no notification system, and NO NEW ROW. That last part is the point:
a feature that exists because vertical space is scarce must not spend vertical
space explaining itself, and FirstTimeHint is an absolute overlay that costs none.

  app/components/teachingRegistry.ts    narrative_expand_v1, first in the
                                        exploration group
  app/screens/ExplorationScreen.tsx     the derivation hoisted; one candidate
                                        `{ id: …narrative_expand_v1.id, when:
                                        !modalOwnsBeat && narrativeConstrained &&
                                        !narrativeReaderOpen }`

EVERY ONE OF THE OWNER'S EIGHT RULES IS HELD, AND THE SUITE HOLDS THEM. No device
or model check (§B, which also proves a LARGE 430×932 viewport still teaches when
its feed is squeezed). No raw screen-size rule — the real measured constraint or
nothing (§A, §C, §I). No permanent vertical cost: the card is an absolute overlay,
`styles.feed` and `styles.controls` are byte-identical, and there is still exactly
one card site on the screen (§D). The reader is not auto-opened (§E). Its content
and architecture are untouched (§E, §I). No narrative state moves — gameLog,
screen, coin and clock all unchanged across raise and dismissal (§H). It does not
nag: taught once per install, and four later constraint transitions say nothing
(§F). EXPAND remains the durable signal and still opens the reader with the card
dismissed (§E).

THE COPY NAMES THE CONTROL THE RAIL ACTUALLY DRAWS, and the suite reads that label
out of the screen rather than trusting the string — if the key is ever renamed and
the card is not, §A goes red instead of the player being told to tap something that
no longer exists.

  ota1880TheConstraintTeachesItsDoor   29/29 — registry shape and replay, label
                                       drift, wiring, device-independence, the
                                       threshold on both sides, zero layout cost,
                                       no auto-open, no nag, per-install
                                       persistence, accessibility, state
                                       invariance, the OTA-1878 contract
  related + named contracts            11 suites, 225/225 (1880, 1878, 1879,
                                       1803, 1485, 1246, 1255, 1799, 1738 ×2,
                                       1806)
  fast surface                         1379/1379 suites · 16,107 passed ·
                                       3 skipped
  typecheck:ci                         exit 0
  typecheck:tests                      OK — at baseline (196), no growth
  lint                                 clean
  check gates                          22/22

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, none committed, both production files restored
byte-identically (md5 verified). NC1 drop `narrativeConstrained` from the gate so
the card raises always — 6 red, the whole of §C plus the wiring pin. NC2 key the
gate on `Platform.OS` instead — 6 red, including §B's rule that the gate may name
no device, which is the defect class the owner forbade. NC3 remove the card from
the slot entirely — 14 red across §A, §D, §E, §F, §G and §H.

ONE OWNER PREFERENCE IS NOT MET, AND IT IS NOT HIDDEN HERE. The owner described a
transient overlay or callout associated VISUALLY with EXPAND. FirstTimeHint is a
centred full-screen card, not a callout anchored to the rail; no toast or callout
primitive exists in this repo, and building one would be the general-purpose
notification system the owner ruled out. So the card names EXPAND in copy instead
of pointing at it. Whether that topology is acceptable is the owner's call.

FOUR TEST-HARNESS FACTS WORTH RECORDING, all of them in the suite and none in
production. FirstTimeHint's own `Got it` key takes a children FUNCTION (OTA-1806's
press planes), so it cannot be found by its label; the dismissal helper presses the
scrim, which carries the SAME `dismiss` handler, and the visible label is asserted
separately by name. A `style` prop is not necessarily flat and not necessarily a
style — it resolves through StyleSheet.flatten, because a direct `.position` read
misses a value one level down in an array. Two finders had to stop using
JSON.stringify on arbitrary props: somewhere in this tree a node carries a circular
`Provider`, and a finder that throws on an unrelated node never reaches its target.
And `<FirstTimeHint` must be counted WITH its first prop — a bare tag match also
counts the screen's own OTA-1738 prose, which is the OTA-1721 class, where an
instrument acts on a comment that names what it hunts for.

NOT CLAIMED: physical verification on the owner's hardware, and the OTA-1879
DiceRoller proportions remain visually unapproved. Neither is reopened here.
